> A speed release: `inspect` and every app lookup built on it are several times faster on large instances, plus fixes that make `start`, `stop`, and shared-mode installs safer.

### New Features

* `cwcli axi setup-wizard <project> <site>` completes Frappe's setup wizard headlessly, so a freshly created site stops landing in the setup-wizard state (where a non-System-Manager desk renders without its navbar). `cwcli axi init --complete-setup` does the same during provisioning and reports the result in the same init document; `--country`, `--currency`, and `--timezone` set the wizard's defaults. It is idempotent and creates no user.

### Bug Fixes

* `cwcli start` on a frappe container that exits right after starting, or dies partway through the start, now reports a clean "not running" error with the container's exit code and a `docker logs` hint, instead of Docker's raw `409 ... is not running` traceback.
* A shared-mode uid remap can no longer brick an instance: every workspace re-own now runs before the `frappe` user's identity is changed, a failed re-own stops before that change, and the container's main process is held for the length of the remap so it cannot exit halfway through.
* `cwcli stop` now takes MariaDB down last and gives it 60 seconds to shut down, instead of Docker's default (as little as 1 second on Docker Desktop). If the database is still killed before it finishes, `stop` reports the unclean shutdown and exits non-zero rather than claiming a clean stop. `rm` gives the database the same grace period and warns on an unclean shutdown.
* One unreadable bench or site no longer breaks a whole `inspect` or app lookup: its cached rows are kept and marked unverified, with a warning naming the bench or site and the step that failed.
* Bench discovery no longer silently drops every bench under a search path when one subdirectory in it is unreadable.
* `cwcli setup migrate` now completes on an instance holding a real bench; container-only symlinks are copied as links instead of followed.
* `cwcli run -i` without a terminal now waits for its command to finish, instead of returning success while the command keeps running in the background.

### Performance Improvements

* Measured on a 32-bench, 47-site instance, with byte-identical `inspect --json` and `axi inspect` output before and after:
  * A full `inspect` went from about 101 s to about 13 s. Each bench is now read in one container exec with a single Frappe process, instead of one exec per fact and one `bench --site` call per site.
  * A cached `inspect` went from about 22 s to under 1 s, and bench discovery from about 9 s to about 0.1 s.
  * Finding which sites have an app installed (used by `apps update`, `apps checkout`, `apps list --installed`, and `apps install`) went from about 3.5 s to about 0.5 s per bench.
  * The cache refresh after `apps install`/`uninstall`/`checkout`, `update`, `rm-site`, `rm-bench`, and `init` now re-reads only the bench that changed, going from about 52 s to about 1 s. If that refresh fails, the project's cache is cleared so the next read re-inspects instead of serving stale data.
